In most cases, the surrounding context should be enough for the merchant to understand the information in the list. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Listbox" (Anatomy).

author: Shopify
title: Listbox: Best practices
statement: Listboxes should: - Be clearly labeled so it’s noticeable to the merchant what type of options will be available - Limit the number of options displayed at once - Indicate a loading state to the merchant while option data is being populated ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Listbox" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Listbox: Structure
statement: The Listbox component is based on the Aria 1.2 Listbox pattern. It is important to not present interactive elements inside of list box options as they can interfere with navigation for assistive technology users.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Listbox" (Accessibility > Structure).

author: Shopify
title: Listbox: Keyboard support
statement: - Access the list of options with the up and down arrow keys - Select an option that has focus with the enter / return key
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Listbox" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Option list: {frontmatter.title}
statement: The option list component lets you create a list of grouped items that merchants can pick from. This can include single selection or multiple selection of options. Option list usually appears in a popover, and sometimes in a modal or a sidebar. Option lists are styled differently than choice lists and should not be used within a form, but as a standalone menu.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Option list" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Option list: Best practices
statement: The option list component should: - Be placed on its own inside a container. Usually the container behaves like a menu, as it does with popover. Don’t place other components within the same container. - Not be used when a select component will do. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Option list" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Option list > Content guidelines > Option lists
title: Option list: Option lists
statement: Each item in an option list should be clear and descriptive.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Option list" (Content guidelines > Option lists).

author: Shopify
title: Option list: Accessibility
statement: Items in an option list are organized as list items ( ) in an unordered list ( ) and are conveyed as a group of related elements to assistive technology users. Controls in simple option lists are buttons, and controls in multiple option lists are checkboxes. If you customize the option list, you can provide ARIA roles that fit the context. These roles must be valid according to the W3C ARIA specification to be conveyed correctly to screen reader users. - The role prop adds an ARIA role to the option list wrapper
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Option list" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Resource item: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Resource items represent specific objects within a collection, such as products or orders. They provide contextual information on the resource type and link to the object’s detail page.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource item" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Resource item: Required components
statement: The resource item component must be wrapped in the resource list component. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource item" (Required components).

author: Shopify
title: Resource item: Accessibility
statement: Resource items function as links to the full-page representations of the items. Each item should have a unique name prop. For each ResourceItem, the accessibilityLabel prop should be used to give the link a unique aria-label value. The aria-label value should convey the link’s purpose, using the name value. Merchants who use screen readers or other text to speech tools should be able to easily distinguish each link from the others. When adding custom content to resource items, ensure that all text is available to all users and that all custom controls have a unique accessible name to help users understand what will happen when the control is activated.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource item" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Resource item: Keyboard
statement: Links can be activated with the enter / return key by default. If you add custom controls to resource items, then make sure that the controls: - Can be used with the keyboard - Receive keyboard focus in a logical order - Display a visible focus indicator ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource item" (Accessibility > Keyboard).

author: Shopify
title: Resource item: Best practices
statement: Resource items should: - Be tailored to the specific type of context being displayed. - Perform an action when clicked. The action should navigate to the resource’s details page or provide more detail about the item. Resource items can optionally: - Provide shortcut actions for quick access to frequent actions from the resource’s details page. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource item" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Resource item: Content guidelines
statement: Resource items should: - Present the information that merchants need to find the items that they’re looking for. - Support merchant tasks for the particular type of resource. - Avoid colons. - Shortcut actions don’t need to follow the full verb + noun formula for buttons. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource item" (Content guidelines).

author: Shopify
title: Resource list: {frontmatter.title}
statement: A resource list displays a collection of objects of the same type, like products or customers. The main job of a resource list is to help merchants find an object and navigate to a full-page representation of it. Resource lists can also: - Support customized list items - Include bulk actions so merchants can act on multiple objects at once - Support sorting and filtering of long lists - Be paired with pagination to make long lists digestible ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource list" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Resource list: Purpose
statement: Shopify is organized around objects that represent merchants businesses, like customers, products, and orders. Each individual order, for example, is given a dedicated page that can be linked to. In Shopify, we call these types of objects resources, and we call the object’s dedicated page its details page.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource list" (Purpose).

author: Shopify
title: Resource list: Problem
statement: Take orders as an example. Merchants may have a lot of them. They need a way to scan their orders, see what state they’re in and find out which ones need action first. In other words, they need a way find an individual order, call up more information about it, and take action on it.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource list" (Purpose > Problem).

author: Shopify
title: Resource list: Solution
statement: Resource lists function as: - A content format, presenting a set of individual resources in a compact form - A system for taking action on one or more individual resources - A way to navigate to an individual resource’s details page Because a details page displays all the content and actions for an individual resource, you can think of a resource list as a summary of these details pages. In this way resource lists bridge a middle level in Shopify’s navigation hierarchy.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource list" (Purpose > Solution).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Resource list > Purpose > A resource list isn’t a data table
title: Resource list: A resource list isn’t a data table
statement: On wide screens, a resource list often looks like a table, especially if some content is aligned in columns. Despite this, resource lists and data tables have different purposes. A data table is a form of data visualization. It works best to present highly structured data for comparison and analysis. If your use case is more about visualizing or analyzing data, use the data table component. If your use case is more about finding and taking action on objects, use a resource list. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource list" (Purpose > A resource list isn’t a data table).

author: Shopify
title: Resource list: Best practices
statement: Resource lists can live in many places in Shopify. You could include a short resource list in a card summarizing recent marketing activities. You could also dedicate an entire page to a resource list like Shopify’s main products list. Resource lists should: - Have items that perform an action when clicked. The action should navigate to the resource’s details page or otherwise provide more detail about the item. - Customize the content and layout of their list items to support merchants’ needs. - Support sorting if the list can be long, and especially if different merchant tasks benefit from different sort orders. - Support filtering if the list can be long. - Paginate when the current list contains more than 50 items. - Use the skeleton page component on initial page load for the rest of the page if the loading prop is true and items are processing. Resource lists can optionally: - Provide bulk actions for tasks that are often applied to many list items at once. For example, merchants may want to add the same tag to a large number of products. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource list" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Resource list: Content guidelines
statement: Resource lists should: - Identify the type of resource, usually with a heading
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource list" (Content guidelines).

author: Shopify
title: Resource list: Don’t
statement: - No heading - Indicate when not all members of a resource are being shown. For a card summarizing and linking to recently purchased products:
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource list" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Resource list: Don’t
statement: - Products - Follow the verb + noun formula for bulk actions - Follow the content guidelines for filter options and applied filters ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Resource list" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Footer help: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Footer help is used to refer merchants to more information related to the product or feature they’re using.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Footer help" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Footer help: Best practices
statement: Footer help should: - Be positioned at the bottom of the interface - Provide links to help that’s related to the experience on the screen - Not be used to promote features or provide explanations for how something works - Never link to information designed to upsell to merchants - In rare cases, link to blog posts when there isn’t any help documentation to help merchants with the most logical next step in the workflow It’s recommended to link your footer help component to help documentation. Linking directly to your contact information might result in receiving a higher number of emails or calls. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Footer help" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Footer help > Content guidelines > Footer help
title: Footer help
statement: By default, footer help should link to information in the Shopify Help Center and should follow this content pattern: - Learn more about \{X\} Links should be: Clearly labeled: Merchants shouldn’t need to guess where they’ll end up if they click on an action link. Never use “click here” as a link because it doesn’t set expectations about what’s next. Links should not be: Marked as external: Do not set the external prop on the Link component to force open a new tab.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Footer help" (Content guidelines > Footer help).

author: Shopify
title: Footer help: Do
statement: - Learn more about [shipping zones] - [Contact us] about email marketing
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Footer help" (Content guidelines > Do).

author: Shopify
title: Footer help: Don’t
statement: - Go to [docs] to learn about zones. - Find out about [themes]. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Footer help" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Navigation: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Access resources and move between sections, pages, or views in a structured and intuitive way.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Navigation" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Link: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Links take users to another place, and usually appear within or directly following a sentence.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Link > Best practices > Buttons versus links
title: Link: Buttons versus links
statement: Links are used primarily for navigation, and usually appear within or directly following a sentence. Buttons are used primarily for actions, such as “Add”, “Close”, “Cancel”, or “Save”. Plain buttons, which look similar to links, are used for less important or less commonly used actions, such as “view shipping settings”. The HTML that renders for the Button and Link components carries meaning. Using these components intentionally and consistently results in: - a more inclusive experience for assistive technology users - a more cohesive visual experience for sighted users - products that are easier to maintain at scale
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Best practices > Buttons versus links).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Link > Best practices > Open a new tab only when necessary
title: Link: Open a new tab only when necessary
statement: Use default links whenever possible to avoid disorienting merchants and causing accessibility problems by opening a new tab. External links should be used when merchants are: - Performing a task or workflow, like creating a product - Navigating to a page outside of the Shopify admin
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Best practices > Open a new tab only when necessary).

author: Shopify
title: Link: No icon
statement: Avoid using the external icon, as it can add unnecessary visual load inside a sentence or when accompanied by other content. Instead, add clarity to external links through clear link text and predictable placement of the link in a merchant’s workflow. Edge cases: External icons should not be used to indicate a new tab or window is being opened. However, they may be used sparingly in features where symbols help merchants scan and pick from a list of several kinds of navigation options, like the admin's global search results.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Best practices > No icon).

author: Shopify
title: Link: Do
statement: Instead of using an external icon, consider using an icon with more meaning to strenghten your message
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Best practices > Do).

author: Shopify
title: Link: Unstyled links
statement: If the existing link styles don’t meet the needs of your project, then use the UnstyledLink component to create a custom link style. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Best practices > Unstyled links).

author: Shopify
title: Link: Content guidelines
statement: The link component should follow the content guidelines for links. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Content guidelines).

author: Shopify
title: Link: Accessibility
statement: Use the url prop to give the link component a valid href value. This allows the element to be identified as a link to assistive technologies and gives it default keyboard support. The Link component is underlined to give interactive elements a shape. This allows links to not rely on color from being the only way users can tell if an element is interactive.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Link: Do
statement: - Remove the link underline when link is repeated in a list or navigation - Use underlines for links when used inline content
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Accessibility > Do).

author: Shopify
title: Link: Don’t
statement: - Remove underlines when the user cannot determine it's interactivity
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Accessibility > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Link: Submitting data
statement: Merchants generally expect links to navigate, and not to submit data or take action. If you need a component that doesn’t have a URL associated with it, then use the button component instead.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Accessibility > Submitting data).

author: Shopify
title: Link: Labeling
statement: Give links text that clearly describes their purpose. The accessibilityLabel prop adds an aria-label attribute to the link, which can be accessed by assistive technologies like screen readers. Typically, this label text replaces the visible text on the link for merchants who use assistive technology. To provide consistency and clarity: - Use the same text for links that navigate to the same content - Use different text for links that navigate to different content
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Accessibility > Labeling).

author: Shopify
title: Link: Keyboard support
statement: Links use browser defaults for keyboard interaction. - Give links keyboard focus with the tab key (or shift + tab when tabbing backwards) - Activate links with the enter / return key
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Link" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Pagination: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Use pagination to let merchants move through an ordered collection of items that has been split into pages. On the web, pagination uses buttons to move back and forth between pages. On iOS and Android, pagination uses infinite scrolling.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Pagination" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Pagination: Best practices
statement: On all platforms, pagination should: - Only be used for lists with more than 25 items Web pagination should: - Be placed at the bottom of a long list that has been split up into pages - Pagination should navigate to the previous and next set of items in the paged list - Hint when merchants are at the first or the last page by disabling the corresponding button iOS and Android pagination should: - Start loading items when merchants are close to the bottom, roughly 5 items from the end - Show a spinner below the list to indicate that items have been requested ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Pagination" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Tabs: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Use to alternate among related views within the same context.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tabs" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Tabs: Best practices
statement: Tabs should: - Represent the same kind of content, such as a list-view with different filters applied. Don’t use tabs to group content that is dissimilar. - Only be active one at a time. - Not force merchants to jump back and forth to do a single task. Merchants should be able to complete their work and find what they need under each tab. - Not be used for primary navigation. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tabs" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Tabs
statement: Tabs should: - Be clearly labeled to help differentiate the different sections beneath them. - Have short and scannable labels, generally kept to single word. - Relate to the section of Shopify they’re on. Imagine the page section title is an invisible noun after the tab. For example, the tabs for the orders section are: - All - Open - Unfulfilled - Unpaid The tabs for the gift cards section are: - All - New - Partially used - Used - Disabled And for the customers section, the tabs are: - All - New - Returning - Abandoned checkouts - Email subscribers Where possible, follow this pattern when writing tabs.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tabs" (Content guidelines > Tabs).

author: Shopify
title: Overlays: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Display contextual elements on top of the main admin interface that provide additional information or functionality.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Overlays" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Popover: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Popovers are small overlays that open on demand. They let merchants access additional content and actions without cluttering the page.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Popover" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Popover: Best practices
statement: Popovers should: - Always be positioned next to the button or other interface element that triggers them - Be used for secondary or less important information and actions since they’re hidden until merchants hit the trigger - Contain navigation or actions that share a relationships to each other - Be triggered by a clearly labeled button - Use a default or tertiary button as the activator ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Popover" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Popover: Popover content
statement: If a popover contains actions, they should: - Be clear and predictable: merchants should be able to anticipate what will happen when they click on an action item. Never deceive merchants by mislabeling an action.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Popover" (Content guidelines > Popover content).

author: Shopify
title: Popover: Don’t
statement: - New order - Buy - Be action-led: buttons should always lead with a strong verb that encourages action. To provide enough context to merchants use the \{verb\}+\{noun\} format on buttons except in the case of common actions like Save, Close, Cancel, or OK.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Popover" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Popover: Don’t
statement: - HTML editing options - File name changes - Duplicate this order so that you can make edits, updates, or changes - Be scannable, especially when the popover contains a list of actions or options. Avoid unnecessary words and articles such as “the”, “an”, or “a”.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Popover" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Popover: Don’t
statement: - Add a menu item If the popover includes a series of navigational links, each item should: - Be concise but still give merchants enough information so they can easily find and accurately navigate to the path they want.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Popover" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Popover: Accessibility
statement: Popovers usually contain an option list or an action list, but can also contain other controls or content. To assist screen readers with sending focus to an action list, pass autofocusTarget='first-node' to Popover. This will avoid known issues a screen reader may have with keyboard support once focus is moved off the activator. Web browsers assign a default value of 'menu' to the aria-haspopup role. You can use the prop ariaHaspopup to specify a value. Screen readers may fail to send focus to the Popover content when they expect the content to be adjacent to the element with aria-haspopup in the DOM tree. In this scenario, it is recommended not to provide the ariaHaspopup prop.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Popover" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Popover: Keyboard support
statement: - When a popover opens, focus moves to the first focusable element or to the popover container - Once focus is in the popover, merchants can access controls in the popover using the tab key (and shift + tab backwards) and standard keystrokes for interacting - Merchants can dismiss the popover by tabbing out of it, pressing the esc key, or clicking outside of it - When the popover is closed, focus returns to the element that launched it
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Popover" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Tooltip: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Tooltips are floating labels that briefly explain the function of a user interface element. They can be triggered when merchants hover, focus, tap, or click.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tooltip" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Tooltip: Best practices
statement: Tooltips should: - Provide useful, additional information or clarification. - Succinctly describe or expand on the element they point to. - Be provided for icon-only buttons or a button with an associated keyboard shortcut. - Not be used to communicate critical information, including errors in forms or other interaction feedback. - Not contain any links or buttons. - Be used sparingly. If you’re building something that requires a lot of tooltips, work on clarifying the design and the language in the experience. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tooltip" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Tooltip: Basic tooltips
statement: Tooltips should: - Be written in sentence case - Be concise and scannable - Not be used to communicate error messages or important account information
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tooltip" (Content guidelines > Basic tooltips).

author: Shopify
title: Tooltip: Do
statement: Post reach is the number of people who have seen your post in their News Feed.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tooltip" (Content guidelines > Do).

author: Shopify
title: Tooltip: Don’t
statement: To continue using Shopify, this amount must be paid immediately. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tooltip" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Autocomplete: {frontmatter.title}
statement: The autocomplete component is an input field that provides selectable suggestions as a merchant types into it. It allows merchants to quickly search through and select from large collections of options. It's a convenience wrapper around the Combobox and Listbox components with minor UI differences.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Autocomplete" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Autocomplete: Best practices
statement: The autocomplete component should: - Be clearly labeled so it’s obvious to the merchant what type of options will be available - Limit the number of options displayed at once - Not be used within a popover - Indicate a loading state to the merchant while option data is being populated ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Autocomplete" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Autocomplete: Content guidelines
statement: The input field for autocomplete should follow the content guidelines for text fields. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Autocomplete" (Content guidelines).

author: Shopify
title: Autocomplete: Structure
statement: The autocomplete component is based on the ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern and the Aria 1.2 Listbox pattern. The autocomplete list displays below the text field or other control by default so it is easy for merchants to discover and use. However, you can change the position with the preferredPosition prop. Autocomplete features can be challenging for merchants with visual, motor, and cognitive disabilities. Even when they’re built using best practices, these features can be difficult to use with some assistive technologies. Merchants should always be able to search, enter data, or perform other activities without relying on the autocomplete.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Autocomplete" (Accessibility > Structure).

author: Shopify
title: Autocomplete: Do
statement: Use autocomplete as progressive enhancement to make the interface easier to use for most merchants.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Autocomplete" (Accessibility > Do).

author: Shopify
title: Autocomplete: Don’t
statement: Require that merchants make a selection from the autocomplete to complete a task.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Autocomplete" (Accessibility > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Autocomplete: Keyboard support
statement: - Give the autocomplete text input keyboard focus with the tab key (or shift + tab when tabbing backwards) - Access the list of options with the up and down arrow keys - Select an option that has focus with the enter / return key
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Autocomplete" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Checkbox: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Checkboxes are most commonly used to give merchants a way to make a range of selections (zero, one, or multiple). They may also be used as a way to have merchants indicate they agree to specific terms and services.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Checkbox" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Checkbox: Best practices
statement: Checkboxes should: - Work independently from each other. Selecting one checkbox shouldn’t change the selection status of another checkbox in the list. The exception is when a checkbox is used to make a bulk selection of multiple items. - Be framed positively. For example, say “Publish store” instead of “Hide store”. - Always have a label when used to activate or deactivate a setting. - Be listed according to a logical order, whether it’s alphabetical, numerical, time-based, or some other clear system. - Link to more information or include a subtitle as required to provide more explanation. Don’t rely on tooltips to explain a checkbox. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Checkbox" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Checkbox > Content guidelines > Lists with checkboxes
title: Checkbox: Lists with checkboxes
statement: Lists that use checkboxes should: - Start with a capital letter
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Checkbox" (Content guidelines > Lists with checkboxes).

author: Shopify
title: Checkbox: Don’t
statement: - option 1 - option 2 - option 3 - Not use commas or semicolons at the end of each line
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Checkbox" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Checkbox: Don’t
statement: - Red; - Yellow; - Blue. - In the rare case where the checkbox is asking merchants to agree to terms or service, use the first person
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Checkbox" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Checkbox: Accessibility
statement: Screen readers convey the state of the checkbox automatically. - Use the disabled prop to apply the HTML disabled attribute to the checkbox . This prevents merchants from being able to interact with the checkbox, and conveys its inactive state to assistive technologies. - Use the id prop to provide a unique id attribute value for the checkbox. If an id isn’t provided, then the component generates one. All checkboxes must have unique id values to work correctly with assistive technologies. - Setting checked="indeterminate" conveys the state of the checkbox using aria-checked="mixed". - Setting the ariaControls prop conveys the ID of the element whose contents or presence are controlled by the checkbox to screen reader users with the aria-controls attribute.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Checkbox" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Checkbox: Labeling
statement: - The required label prop conveys the purpose of the checkbox to all merchants - Use the labelHidden prop to visually hide the label but make it available to assistive technologies - When you provide help text via the helpText prop or an inline error message via the error prop, the help or error content is conveyed to screen reader users with the aria-describedby attribute
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Checkbox" (Accessibility > Labeling).

author: Shopify
title: Checkbox: Keyboard support
statement: - Move focus to each checkbox using the tab key (or shift + tab when tabbing backwards) - To interact with the checkbox when it has keyboard focus, press the space key
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Checkbox" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Choice list: {frontmatter.title}
statement: A choice list lets you create a list of grouped radio buttons or checkboxes. Use this component if you need to group together a related list of interactive choices.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Choice list" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Choice list: Best practices
statement: Choice lists should: - Include a title that tells merchants what to do or explains the available options - Label options clearly based on what the option will do - Avoid mutually exclusive options when allowing multiple selection ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Choice list" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Choice list > Content guidelines > List titles
title: Choice list: List titles
statement: List titles should: - Help merchants understand how the items in the list are grouped together, or should explain what kind of choice merchants are making
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Choice list" (Content guidelines > List titles).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Choice list > Content guidelines > Be concise and scannable
title: Choice list: Be concise and scannable
statement: - Use simple, clear language that can be read at a glance - Keep list titles to a single sentence - It the title introduces the list, it should end with a colon - Should be written in sentence case
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Choice list" (Content guidelines > Be concise and scannable).

author: Shopify
title: Choice list: Do
statement: If the customer abandons their checkout, send them an email reminder to complete their order: - Option a - Option b
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Choice list" (Content guidelines > Do).

author: Shopify
title: Choice list: Don’t
statement: If the customer abandons their checkout, send them an email reminder to complete their order - Option a - Option b
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Choice list" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Choice list > Content guidelines > List choices
title: Choice list: List choices
statement: Every item in a choice list should: - Start with a capital letter - Not use commas or semicolons at the end of each line - Be written in sentence case (the first word capitalized, the rest lowercase)
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Choice list" (Content guidelines > List choices).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Choice list > Content guidelines > Helper text and descriptions
title: Choice list: Helper text and descriptions
statement: If your list contains helper text, only the description below the list item should contain punctuation. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Choice list" (Content guidelines > Helper text and descriptions).

author: Shopify
title: Choice list: Accessibility
statement: The choice list component uses the accessibility features of the checkbox and radio button components.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Choice list" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Color picker: {frontmatter.title}
statement: The color picker is used to let merchants select a color visually. For example, merchants use the color picker to customize the accent color of the email templates for their shop.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Color picker" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Color picker: Best practices
statement: - Use the alpha slider if you want to allow merchants to be able to select a transparent color
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Color picker" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Combobox: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Combobox is an accessible autocomplete input that enables merchants to filter a list of options and select one or more values.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Combobox" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Combobox: Anatomy
statement: A combobox is made up of the following: 1. TextField: A text input that activates a popover displaying a list of options. As merchants type in the text field, the list of options is filtered by the input value. Options replace or add to the input value when selected. 2. Popover: An overlay containing a list of options. 3. Listbox: A list of options to filter and select or deselect. 4. Listbox.Option: The individual options to select or deselect. Check out the listbox component documentation to learn how to compose it with various content. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Combobox" (Anatomy).

author: Shopify
title: Combobox: Best practices
statement: The Combobox component should: - Be clearly labeled so the merchant knows what kind of options will be available - Not be used within a popover - Indicate a loading state to the merchant while option data is being populated - Order items in an intentional way so it’s easy for the merchant to find a specific value ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Combobox" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Combobox: Content guidelines
statement: The input field for Combobox should follow the content guidelines for text fields. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Combobox" (Content guidelines).

author: Shopify
title: Combobox: Sorting
statement: Item order should be intentional. Order them so it’s easy for the merchant to find a specific value. Some ways you can do this: - Sort options in alphabetical order - Display options based on how frequently the merchant selects an option If multiple options can be selected, move selected items to the top of the list. If this doesn’t work for your context, you can override this behavior.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Combobox" (Sorting and filtering > Sorting).

author: Shopify
title: Combobox: Filtering
statement: - By default, menu items are filtered based on whether or not they match the value of the textfield. - Filters are not case-sensitive by default. - You can apply custom filtering logic if the default behavior doesn’t make sense for your use case. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Combobox" (Sorting and filtering > Filtering).

author: Shopify
title: Combobox: Tags autocomplete
statement: The tag multi-select input enables merchants to efficiently add or remove tags from a resource, like a product or an order. It uses the inline autocomplete combobox pattern to present merchants with an editable list of tags to browse and select from. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Combobox" (Patterns > Tags autocomplete).

author: Shopify
title: Combobox: Structure
statement: The Combobox component is based on the ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern. It is a combination of a single-line TextField and a Popover. The current implementation expects a Listbox component to be used. The Combobox popover displays below the text field or other control by default so it is easy for merchants to discover and use. However, you can change the position with the preferredPosition prop. Combobox features can be challenging for merchants with visual, motor, and cognitive disabilities. Even when they’re built using best practices, these features can be difficult to use with some assistive technologies. Merchants should always be able to search, enter data, or perform other activities without relying on the combobox.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Combobox" (Accessibility > Structure).

author: Shopify
title: Combobox: Do
statement: - Use combobox as progressive enhancement to make the interface easier to use for most merchants.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Combobox" (Accessibility > Do).

author: Shopify
title: Combobox: Don’t
statement: - Require that merchants make a selection from the combobox to complete a task.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Combobox" (Accessibility > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Combobox: Keyboard support
statement: - Give the combobox's text input keyboard focus with the tab key (or shift + tab when tabbing backwards)
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Combobox" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Date picker: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Date pickers let merchants choose dates from a visual calendar that’s consistently applied wherever dates need to be selected across Shopify. Check out the new patterns section to learn how merchants prefer to select dates in different scenarios!
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Date picker" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Date picker: Best practices
statement: Date pickers should: - Use smart defaults and highlight common selections - Close after a single date is selected unless a range with a start and end date is required - Set the start date on first click or tap and the end date on second click or tap if a range is required - Not be used to enter a date that is many years in the future or the past - Follow date format guidelines ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Date picker" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Date picker: Accessibility
statement: Some users might find interacting with date pickers to be challenging. When you use the date picker component, always give users the option to enter the date using a text field component as well. If you use the date picker within a popover component, then use a button to trigger the popover instead of displaying the popover when the text input gets focus. This gives users more control over their experience.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Date picker" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Date picker: Keyboard support
statement: - Press the tab key to move forward and shift + tab to move backward through the previous button, next button, and the calendar - When focus is in the calendar, move keyboard focus between the dates using the arrow keys - To select a date that has focus, press the enter / return key
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Date picker" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Drop zone: {frontmatter.title}
statement: The drop zone component lets users upload files by dragging and dropping the files into an area on a page, or activating a button.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Drop zone" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Drop zone > Best practices > Drop zone
title: Drop zone
statement: Drop zones should: - Inform merchants when the file(s) can’t be uploaded: - When possible, use validation errors on drag to detect and explain things like file size limits or file types accepted. - Use the banner component with a critical status to communicate errors that happen on the server. - Provide feedback once the file(s) have been dropped and uploading begins. - For convenience, allow files to be dropped anywhere on the page by enabling dropOnPage. - Provide a file upload button to allow merchants to select files for upload in a traditional way. Do this by using the DropZone.FileUpload subcomponent.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Drop zone" (Best practices > Drop zone).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Drop zone > Best practices > Validation errors
title: Drop zone: Validation errors
statement: The drop zone component validates file type by default. File types you wish to accept can be defined by editing the accept property. This component also accepts custom validations using the customValidator property. When validation fails, the component sets itself to error mode. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Drop zone" (Best practices > Validation errors).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Drop zone > Content guidelines > Client-side validation error messages
title: Drop zone: Client-side validation error messages
statement: Client-side validation errors give instant feedback. Validation error messages should be: - Explicit: help merchants understand why their file can’t be uploaded and what they should change to successfully upload their file - In sentence case: capitalize only the first word in the message - Concise: use simple, clear language that can be read at a glance. For example: File size must be less than 20MB File type must be .gif, .jpg, .png or .svg
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Drop zone" (Content guidelines > Client-side validation error messages).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Drop zone > Content guidelines > Server-side upload error messages
title: Drop zone: Server-side upload error messages
statement: Server-side upload errors give feedback after file submission. Upload error messages should: - Be displayed as a banner with a critical status - Show the name of the file(s) that were not uploaded successfully - Describe why the file(s) couldn’t be uploaded and what merchants should change to upload their file successfully, as seen below ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Drop zone" (Content guidelines > Server-side upload error messages).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Drop zone > Drop zone file upload
title: Drop zone: Drop zone file upload
statement: Use file upload with the drop zone component to let merchants select files for upload in a traditional way.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Drop zone" (Drop zone file upload).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Drop zone > Drop zone file upload > File upload properties
title: Drop zone: File upload properties
statement: ; Prop ; Type ; Description ; Default ; ; actionTitle; string; String that appears in file upload; 'Add file' ; actionHint ; string; String that appears in file upload; 'or drop files to upload'
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Drop zone" (Drop zone file upload > File upload properties).

author: Shopify
title: Drop zone: Accessibility
statement: The drop zone component builds on the native HTML element. It includes a visual as well as a drag and drop area that can receive keyboard focus.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Drop zone" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Drop zone: Keyboard support
statement: To upload a file with the keyboard, merchants can interact with the drag-and-drop region. - To give the input keyboard focus, use the tab key (or shift + tab when tabbing backwards) - To activate the input, use the enter / return or space keys
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Drop zone" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Filters: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Filters is a composite component that filters the items of a list or table. Merchants use filters to: - view different subsets of items in a list or table - filter by typing into a text field - filter by selecting filters or promoted filters The way that merchants interact with filters depends on the components that you decide to incorporate. In its simplest form, filters includes a text field and a set of filters, which can be displayed in different ways. What the filters are and how they’re exposed to merchants is flexible. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Filters" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Filters: Accessibility
statement: The filters component relies on the accessibility features of multiple other components: - Text field - Button - Popover
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Filters" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Filters > Accessibility > Maintain accessibility with custom features
title: Filters: Maintain accessibility with custom features
statement: Since custom HTML can be passed to the component for additional actions, ensure that the filtering system you build is accessible as a whole. All merchants must: - be able to identify and understand labels for all controls - be notified of state changes - be able to complete all actions with the keyboard ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Filters" (Accessibility > Maintain accessibility with custom features).

author: Shopify
title: Filters: Best practices
statement: The filters component should: - help reduce merchant effort by promoting the filtering categories that are most commonly used - include no more than 2 or 3 promoted filters - consider small screen sizes when designing the interface for each filter and the total number filters to include - use children only for content that’s related or relevant to filtering ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Filters" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Filters: Text field
statement: The text field should be clearly labeled so it’s obvious to merchants what they should enter into the field.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Filters" (Content guidelines > Text field).

author: Shopify
title: Filters: Filter badges
statement: Use the name of the filter if the purpose of the name is clear on its own. For example, when you see a filter badge that reads Fulfilled, it’s intuitive that it falls under the Fulfillment status category.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Filters" (Content guidelines > Filter badges).

author: Shopify
title: Filters: Don’t
statement: - Fulfillment: Fulfilled, Unfulfilled If the filter name is ambiguous on its own, add a descriptive word related to the status. For example, Low doesn’t make sense out of context. Add the word “risk” so that merchants know it’s from the Risk category.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Filters" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Filters: Don’t
statement: - (Unfulfilled) (fulfilled) If all tag pills selected: truncate in the middle
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Filters" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Form: Best practices
statement: The form component should be used to: - Wrap around all form input elements - Emulate the native HTML form element behavior with a custom onSubmit callback ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Form" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Form: Accessibility
statement: The form component wraps content in an HTML element. This helps to support assistive technologies that use different interaction and browse modes. Forms can have only one submit button and it must be at the end of the form. By default, buttons added to the form are given a type attribute set to button to avoid conflicts. To make a button the submit button instead (type="submit"), set the submit prop on the button.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Form" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Form: Keyboard support
statement: By default, the implicitSubmit prop is set to true. This allows merchants to submit the form with the enter / return key when focus is in any text field inside the form. This provides a shortcut for keyboard users. If this behavior doesn’t fit the form, then set the prop to false.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Form" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Index filters: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Use index filters to allow merchants to filter, search, and sort their index table data and create unique saved views from the results. Merchants use filters to: - Create different subsets of list items - Search list items by typing a query into the text input - Sort list items by column The way that merchants interact with index filters depends on the components that you decide to incorporate. It supports configuration of a search query input, sorting options, and one or more filters that can be made up of different inputs. Merchants use the tabs in index tables to: - Control which view is visible - Edit the applied filters and search terms of a view - Create, rename, duplicate, or delete views You can create views and control which actions can be performed on a particular view.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Index filters" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Index filters: Anatomy
statement: Index filters are made up of the following: 1. Tabs: A list of saved views. Each tab represents a subset of the list that has been sorted, filtered, and or queried and saved with a unique name. New views can be created directly from the tab list, or by editing the filters, query, or sort selection of an existing view and saving it as new. 2. Search and filter, and sort buttons: The search and filter button allows merchants to toggle the index table from "View" mode to "Filter" mode. When clicked, the button reveals the search field and the filters that allow merchants to edit or create saved views. The sort button activates a popover displaying a list of options merchants can choose from to sort the list items. Merchants can also choose whether the list should be sorted in ascending or descending order. 3. Filters: A set of useful ways to narrow down the list based on the common actions merchants may need to take on the data. The filters should present merchants with form inputs that help them include or exclude list items from the view based on their data. 4. Action buttons: Primary and secondary actions that a merchant can take on the current view. The primary action will always be either "Save" or "Save as" depending on whether the view is mutable, and the secondary action will always be "Cancel". ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Index filters" (Anatomy).

author: Shopify
title: Index filters: Accessibility
statement: The filters component relies on the accessibility features of several other components: - Popover - ChoiceList - Modal - Tabs - Tooltip
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Index filters" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Index filters > Accessibility > Maintain accessibility with custom features
title: Index filters: Maintain accessibility with custom features
statement: Since custom HTML can be passed to the component for additional actions, ensure that the filtering system you build is accessible as a whole. All merchants must be able to: - Identify and understand the labels of all controls - Be notified of state changes as they use the filter controls - Complete all actions using a keyboard ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Index filters" (Accessibility > Maintain accessibility with custom features).

author: Shopify
title: Index filters: Best practices
statement: Index filters should: - Reduce merchant effort by promoting the filtering categories that are most commonly used - Include no more than 2 or 3 promoted filters - Consider small screen sizes when designing the interface for each filter and the total number filters to include - Use children only for content that’s related or relevant to filtering ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Index filters" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Index filters > Content guidelines > Text field
title: Index filters: Text field
statement: The text field should be clearly labeled so it’s obvious to merchants what they should enter into the field.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Index filters" (Content guidelines > Text field).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Index filters > Content guidelines > Filter badges
title: Index filters: Filter badges
statement: Use the name of the filter if the purpose of the name is clear on its own. For example, when you see a filter badge that reads Fulfilled, it’s intuitive that it falls under the Fulfillment status category.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Index filters" (Content guidelines > Filter badges).

author: Shopify
title: Index filters: Don’t
statement: - Fulfillment: Fulfilled, Unfulfilled If the filter name is ambiguous on its own, add a descriptive word related to the status. For example, Low doesn’t make sense out of context. Add the word “risk” so that merchants know it’s from the Risk category.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Index filters" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Index filters: Don’t
statement: - (Unfulfilled) (fulfilled) If all tag pills selected: truncate in the middle
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Index filters" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Selection and input: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Choose or enter information using elements like checkboxes, text fields, and more.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Selection and input" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Inline error: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Inline errors are brief, in-context messages that tell merchants something went wrong with a single or group of inputs in a form. Use inline errors to help merchants understand why a form input may not be valid and how to fix it.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Inline error" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Inline error: Best practices
statement: Inline errors should: - Be brief - Be written in sentence case - Be visible immediately upon a form input that is not valid - Be removed as soon as the input is valid so merchants can immediately tell they fixed the issue - Describe specific solutions so merchants can successfully complete their task in the form - Not be placed out of context of the input or group of inputs they describe Learn more about error message patterns ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Inline error" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Inline error > Content guidelines > Inline error messages
title: Inline error: Inline error messages
statement: Since the error message is directly below the source of the problem, the copy only needs to explain why the error happened. Optionally, the message can clarify what to do next or offer a one-click fix. Inline error messages should: - Clearly explain what went wrong, give a next step, or offer a one-click fix - Be short and concise, no more than a single sentence - Use passive voice so merchants don’t feel like they’re being blamed for the error
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Inline error" (Content guidelines > Inline error messages).

author: Shopify
title: Inline error: Accessibility
statement: - Use the required fieldID prop to give the inline error a unique id. This ties the error to a form field using aria-describedby so that it's conveyed to screen reader users. - Use the required message prop to provide the text that describes the error. - The inline error icon helps visually identify the error message for merchants who have difficulty seeing colors or who use settings that remove color from the page.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Inline error" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Radio button: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Use radio buttons to present each item in a list of options where merchants must make a single selection.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Radio button" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Radio button: Best practices
statement: Radio buttons should: - Always be used with an associated label component. - Be part of a list of radio buttons that: - Include at least two or more choices. - Are used to have merchants select only one option. - Include mutually exclusive options—this means that each option must be independent from every other option in the list. For example: Red, blue, and yellow are mutually exclusive. Red, blue, yellow, red/blue are not mutually exclusive. - List options in a rational order that makes logical sense. - Have a default option selected whenever possible. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Radio button" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Radio button > Content guidelines > Radio button labels
title: Radio button: Radio button labels
statement: Radio button labels should: - Be introduced with a colon or a heading - Start with a capital letter
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Radio button" (Content guidelines > Radio button labels).

author: Shopify
title: Radio button: Don’t
statement: - option 1 - Not end in punctuation if it’s a single sentence, word, or a fragment
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Radio button" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Radio button > Content guidelines > Toggle (Android and iOS only)
title: Radio button: Toggle (Android and iOS only)
statement: Toggle labels should: - Be clear what merchants are enabling or disabling - Start with a capital letter Toggle values should: - Never be labeled ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Radio button" (Content guidelines > Toggle (Android and iOS only)).

author: Shopify
title: Radio button: Accessibility
statement: Screen readers convey the state of the radio button automatically. - Use the disabled prop to apply the HTML disabled attribute to the radio button . This prevents merchants from being able to interact with the radio button, and conveys its inactive state to assistive technologies. - Use the id prop to provide a unique id attribute value for the radio button. If an id isn’t provided, then the component generates one. All radio buttons must have unique id values to work correctly with assistive technologies.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Radio button" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Radio button: Labeling
statement: - The required label prop conveys the purpose of the radio button to all merchants - Use the labelHidden prop to visually hide the label but make it available to assistive technologies - When you provide help text via the helpText prop or an inline error message via the error prop, the help or error content is conveyed to screen reader users with the aria-describedby attribute
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Radio button" (Accessibility > Labeling).

author: Shopify
title: Radio button: Keyboard support
statement: - Move focus to the radio button group using the tab key (or shift + tab when tabbing backwards) - Use the up and down arrow keys to change which radio button is selected
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Radio button" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Range slider: {frontmatter.title}
statement: A range slider is an input field that merchants can use to select a numeric value within a given range (minimum and maximum values).
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Range slider" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Range slider: Best practices
statement: Range sliders should: - Always be used with a label, even if that label is hidden. - When a label is visible, it should clearly communicate the purpose of the range input and its values (min, max, step, value) - Be labeled as “Optional” when you need to request input that’s not required - Validate input as soon as merchants have finished interacting with a field (but not before) - Always be used with two text field components when range slider has dual thumbs, to provide accessible alternatives to both the lower and upper thumbs ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Range slider" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Range slider > Content guidelines > Range label
title: Range slider: Range label
statement: A label is a short description of the requested input. Labels are not instructional text but they should be meaningful and clearly indicate what is expected. Labels should be: - Placed above the form field - Short and succinct (1–3 words) - Written in sentence case (the first word capitalized, the rest lowercase)
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Range slider" (Content guidelines > Range label).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Range slider > Content guidelines > Designating optional fields
title: Range slider: Designating optional fields
statement: Try to only ask for information that’s required. If you need to ask merchants to provide optional information, mark the field optional by placing the text “(optional)” at the end of the field’s label. Don’t mark required fields with asterisks.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Range slider" (Content guidelines > Designating optional fields).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Range slider > Content guidelines > Help text
title: Range slider: Help text
statement: Help text provides extra guidance or instruction to people filling out a form field. It can also be used to clarify how the information will be used. As with all form content, help text should be succinct and easy to read.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Range slider" (Content guidelines > Help text).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Range slider > Content guidelines > Validation error messages
title: Range slider: Validation error messages
statement: Error messages should: - Clearly explain what went wrong and how to fix it - Be short and concise, no more than a single sentence - Use passive voice so merchants don’t feel like they’re being blamed for the error
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Range slider" (Content guidelines > Validation error messages).

author: Shopify
title: Range slider: Accessibility
statement: The range slider provides a large click and tap target for the slider thumbs. Merchants can also tap or click on the slider track to move the closest slider thumb.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Range slider" (Accessibility).

author: Shopify
title: Range slider: Single-thumb slider
statement: The default range slider component uses the ARIA 1.1 slider pattern to build upon the default HTML . The required label prop provides a label for the field that’s conveyed to assistive technologies when it receives focus. When the slider is used, the value prop should update visually and programmatically to reflect the current value. To consistently provide the current value to assistive technologies, use the min and max props to provide the minimum and maximum values for the slider.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Range slider" (Accessibility > Single-thumb slider).

author: Shopify
title: Range slider: Dual-thumb slider
statement: The dual-thumb range slider component uses the ARIA 1.1 slider (multi-thumb) pattern. However, the pattern isn’t consistently supported by screen readers, especially on mobile devices. Because of this, it’s best to pair the dual-thumb slider with a set of text fields for each value, or to provide another accessible method for entering information.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Range slider" (Accessibility > Dual-thumb slider).

author: Shopify
title: Range slider: Keyboard
statement: - To move focus to a slider thumb, press the tab key to move forward and or shift + tab to move backward - When a thumb has focus, use the up and down or left and right arrow keys to move the thumb and update the associated value.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Range slider" (Accessibility > Keyboard).

author: Shopify
title: Select: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Select lets merchants choose one option from an options menu. Consider select when you have 4 or more options, to avoid cluttering the interface.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Select" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Select: Best practices
statement: The select component should: - Be used for selecting between 4 or more pre-defined options - Have a default option selected whenever possible - Use “Select” as a placeholder option only if there’s no logical default option ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Select" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Select: Select label
statement: Labels should: - Give a short description (1–3 words) of the requested input. - Be written in sentence case (the first word capitalized, the rest lowercase). - Avoid punctuation and articles (“the”, “an”, “a”). - Be independent sentences. To support internationalization, they should not act as the first part of a sentence that is finished by the component’s options. - Be descriptive, not instructional. If the selection needs more explanation, use help text below the field.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Select" (Content guidelines > Select label).

author: Shopify
title: Tag: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Tags represent a set of interactive, merchant-supplied keywords that help label, organize, and categorize objects. Tags can be added or removed from an object by merchants.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tag" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Tag: Best practices
statement: Tags should: - Be presented close to or within the input control that allows merchants to add and remove tags ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tag" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Tag: Labeling
statement: The button to remove a tag is automatically given a label using aria-label so that screen reader users can distinguish which tag will be removed.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tag" (Accessibility > Labeling).

author: Shopify
title: Tag: Keyboard support
statement: The control to remove a tag is implemented as a button with standard keyboard support. - Give buttons keyboard focus with the tab key (or shift + tab when tabbing backwards) - To activate a button, press the enter / return or space key When a merchant uses the button to remove a tag, it is important to make sure that keyboard focus is managed. Moving focus to the next element in the page is recommended.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Tag" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Text field: {frontmatter.title}
statement: A text field is an input field that merchants can type into. It has a range of options and supports several text formats including numbers.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Text field: Best practices
statement: Text fields should: - Be clearly labeled so it’s obvious to merchants what they should enter into the field - Be labeled as “Optional” when you need to request input that’s not required - Only ask for information that’s really needed - Validate input as soon as merchants have finished interacting with a field (but not before)
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Text field: Autocomplete
statement: The autocomplete attribute in an input field controls two types of browser behavior: 1. Browser autofill: a feature that automatically populates form fields with previously-saved information, such as passwords, addresses, and credit card data. - Autofill is an important feature for our users. Google has found that "users complete forms up to 30% faster" when using autofill. - The WHATWG has a list of supported autofill values for the autocomplete attribute. Review the section "4.10.18.7 Autofill" for all the input types and their corresponding autocomplete attribute values. 2. Browser autocomplete - a feature that displays previously submitted values for that field. - When this is on for a field, a user is presented a list with previously submitted values for the input Recommendation Always add an autocomplete attribute and value to inputs if the type is: color, date, datetime-local, email, month, number, password, range, search, tel, text, time, url, or week.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" (Best practices > Autocomplete).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Text field > Best practices > Turning autofill/autocomplete off
title: Text field: Turning autofill/autocomplete off
statement: Even if you do not want the browser to autofill a user's information, it is recommended you still have an autocomplete attribute with the value off or nope. Unfortunately, not all browsers support or respect autocomplete="off". This makes things challenging. Chrome, for example, has a long outstanding bug and won't add support for off for now. ; Browser; Support for autocomplete="off"; Details ; ; Chrome ; Partial ; Intentionally ignores off value when the user uses the browser's autofill functionality. See bug.; Safari ; Partial ; Ignores off value for username, email and password fields. ; Firefox; Partial ; Ignores off value for login forms. See bug. ; Edge ; Partial ; Intentionally ignores off value when the user uses the browser's autofill functionality. ; Chrome does seem to turn autocomplete off when using the value nope (or any non valid string). However, we have seen some inconsistencies even with that support. Recommendation (Chrome only) - Turning off both autofill and browser autocomplete (previously submitted values) in Chrome - Use autocomplete=nope and also must have a name attribute. - Turning off browser autocomplete (previously submitted values) in Chrome - If you don't have name attribute and the field is not a typical autofill input (address, email, etc), use autocomplete=off.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" (Best practices > Turning autofill/autocomplete off).

author: Shopify
subcategory: Text field > Best practices > Virtual keyboard
title: Text field: Virtual keyboard
statement: The inputMode property should be set to select the appropriate virtual keyboard for the type of data expected to be entered by the user. Above are examples of different number keyboards set with inputMode. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" (Best practices > Virtual keyboard).

author: Shopify
title: Text field: Content guidelines
statement: For text field content guidelines, reference the text fields experience page. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" (Content guidelines).

author: Shopify
title: Text field: Structure
statement: Screen readers convey information about text fields automatically through native HTML. - Use the disabled prop to add the HTML disabled attribute to the text field. - Use the readOnly prop to add the HTML readonly attribute to the text field. - If you use the type prop, then some assistive technologies adapt the software keyboard to the current task. This helps merchants with mobility, vision, and cognitive issues to enter information more easily. Use the id prop to provide a unique id attribute value for the text field. If you don't provide an id, then the component generates one automatically. All text fields need to have unique id values.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" (Accessibility > Structure).

author: Shopify
title: Text field: Labeling
statement: The label prop is required to convey the purpose of the checkbox to all merchants. If there are separate visual cues that convey the purpose of the text field to sighted merchants, then the label can be visually hidden with the labelHidden prop. When you provide help text via the helpText prop or an inline error message via the error prop, the help or error content is conveyed to screen reader users with the aria-describedby attribute. This attribute causes the content to be read along with the label, either immediately or after a short delay. Use the placeholder prop to provide additional instructions. However, don’t rely on placeholders alone since the content isn’t always conveyed to all merchants.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" (Accessibility > Labeling).

author: Shopify
title: Text field: Do
statement: - Use the label to provide instructions critical to using the text field - Use help text and placeholder text to provide additional, non-critical instructions
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" (Accessibility > Do).

author: Shopify
title: Text field: Don’t
statement: Use the placeholder to provide information that’s required to use the text field.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" (Accessibility > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Text field: Keyboard support
statement: Text fields have standard keyboard support. - Merchants who rely on the keyboard expect to move focus to each text field using the tab key (or shift + tab when tabbing backwards) - If the type is set to number, then merchants can use the up and down arrow keys to adjust the value typed into the field when hovering over or focusing the field to make the arrows appear - Using the disabled prop will prevent the text field from receive keyboard focus or inputs - The readOnly prop allows focus on the text field but prevents input or editing - The inputMode prop can be used to bring up a relevant keyboard for merchants on mobile; it’s passed down to the input as an inputmode attribute
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).

author: Shopify
title: Text field: Automatically focusing
statement: Although you can use the autoFocus prop to automatically move focus to the text field, it’s generally best to avoid focusing on fields automatically. The autoFocus prop is set to false by default and should only be used in cases where it won’t force focus to skip other controls or content of equal or greater importance.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Text field" (Accessibility > Automatically focusing).

author: Shopify
title: Data table: {frontmatter.title}
statement: Data tables are used to organize and display all information from a data set. While a data visualization represents part of data set, a data table lets merchants view details from the entire set. This helps merchants compare and analyze the data.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Data table" ({frontmatter.title}).

author: Shopify
title: Data table: Best practices
statement: Data tables should: - Show values across multiple categories and measures. - Allow for filtering and ordering when comparison is not a priority. - Help merchants visualize and scan many values from an entire data set. - Help merchants find other values in the data hierarchy through use of links. - Minimize clutter by only including values that supports the data’s purpose. - Include a summary row to surface the column totals. - Not include calculations within the summary row. - Wrap instead of truncate content. This is because if row titles start with the same word, they’ll all appear the same when truncated. - Not to be used for an actionable list of items that link to details pages. For this functionality, use the resource list component.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Data table" (Best practices).

author: Shopify
title: Data table: Alignment
statement: Column content types are built into the component props so the following alignment rules are followed: - Numerical = Right aligned - Textual data = Left aligned - Align headers with their related data - Don’t center align ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Data table" (Best practices > Alignment).

author: Shopify
title: Data table: Content guidelines
statement: Headers should: - Be informative and descriptive - Concise and scannable - Include units of measurement symbols so they aren’t repeated throughout the columns - Use sentence case (first word capitalized, rest lowercase)
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Data table" (Content guidelines).

author: Shopify
title: Data table: Don’t
statement: Temperature Column content should: - Be concise and scannable - Not include units of measurement symbols (put those symbols in the headers) - Use sentence case (first word capitalized, rest lowercase)
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Data table" (Content guidelines > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Data table: Decimals
statement: Keep decimals consistent. For example, don’t use 3 decimals in one row and 2 in others. ---
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Data table" (Content guidelines > Decimals).

author: Shopify
title: Data table: Structure
statement: Native HTML tables provide a large amount of structural information to screen reader users. Merchants who rely on screen readers can navigate tables and identify relationships between data cells ( ) and headers ( ) using keys specific to their screen reader. Sortable tables use the aria-sort attribute to convey which columns are sortable (and in what direction). They also use aria-label on sorting buttons to convey what activating the button will do.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Data table" (Accessibility > Structure).

author: Shopify
title: Data table: Don’t
statement: Use tables for layout. For a table-like layout that doesn’t use table HTML elements, use the resource list component.
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Data table" (Accessibility > Don’t).

author: Shopify
title: Data table: Keyboard support
statement: Sorting controls for the data table component are implemented with native HTML buttons. - Give buttons keyboard focus with the tab key (or shift + tab when tabbing backwards) - Activate buttons with the enter / return and space keys
citation: Shopify. Shopify Polaris: "Data table" (Accessibility > Keyboard support).
